sanskrit: cakrakūrmāṃ gadānakrāṃ śarakṣudrajhaṣākulām baḍagṛdhrasṛgālānāṃ ghorasaṃghair niṣevitām
english: Its chariot-wheels were its turtles, its maces its crocodiles, and it teemed with arrows for its little fishes; it was haunted by dreadful packs of herons, vultures, and jackals.

sanskrit: nihatān prāṇinaḥ saṃkhye droṇena balinā śaraiḥ vahantīṃ pitṛlokāya śataśo rājasattama
english: O best of kings, it bore by hundreds to the realm of the fathers the living beings whom mighty Droṇa had slain in battle with his arrows.

sanskrit: śarīraśatasaṃbādhāṃ keśaśaivalaśādvalām nadīṃ prāvartayad rājan bhīrūṇāṃ bhayavardhinīm
english: Choked with hundreds of corpses, its weeds and grass the hair of the dead, such a river did he set flowing, O king—a river that swelled the terror of the fearful.

sanskrit: taṃ jayantam anīkāni tāni tāny eva bhārata sarvato 'bhyadravan droṇaṃ yudhiṣṭhirapurogamāḥ
english: As he triumphed thus, O Bhārata, those very armies, with Yudhiṣṭhira at their head, charged upon Droṇa from every side.

sanskrit: tān abhidravataḥ śūrāṃs tāvakā dṛḍhakārmukāḥ sarvataḥ pratyagṛhṇanta tad abhūl lomaharṣaṇam
english: Your warriors, their bows held firm, received those onrushing heroes from every quarter, and the encounter made the hair stand on end.

sanskrit: śatamāyas tu śakuniḥ sahadevaṃ samādravat saniyantṛdhvajarathaṃ vivyādha niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Śakuni of a hundred wiles rushed against Sahadeva and pierced him with whetted arrows, together with his charioteer, his banner, and his car.

sanskrit: tasya mādrīsutaḥ ketuṃ dhanuḥ sūtaṃ hayān api nātikruddhaḥ śaraiś chittvā ṣaṣṭyā vivyādha mātulam
english: The son of Mādrī, not greatly angered, cut down his uncle's banner, bow, charioteer, and horses with his shafts, and pierced him with sixty arrows.

sanskrit: saubalas tu gadāṃ gṛhya pracaskanda rathottamāt sa tasya gadayā rājan rathāt sūtam apātayal
english: But the son of Subala, seizing his mace, leapt down from his splendid chariot, and with that mace, O king, he struck Sahadeva's charioteer from his car.

sanskrit: tatas tau virathau rājan gadāhastau mahābalau cikrīḍatū raṇe śūrau saśṛṅgāv iva parvatau
english: Then those two mighty warriors, O king, both bereft of their chariots, maces in hand, sported in the battle like two peaked mountains.

sanskrit: droṇaḥ pāñcālarājānaṃ viddhvā daśabhir āśugaiḥ bahubhis tena cābhyastas taṃ vivyādha śatādhikaiḥ
english: Droṇa pierced the king of the Pāñcālas with ten swift arrows; and being himself struck by many in return, he pierced that king with more than a hundred.

sanskrit: viviṃśatiṃ bhīmaseno viṃśatyā niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ viddhvā nākampayad vīras tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: Bhīmasena pierced Viviṃśati with twenty whetted arrows, yet the hero could not make him waver, and that seemed a wonder.

sanskrit: viviṃśatis tu sahasā vyaśvaketuśarāsanam bhīmaṃ cakre mahārāja tataḥ sainyāny apūjayan
english: But Viviṃśati at once made Bhīma horseless, bannerless, and bowless, O great king; and thereupon the troops applauded him.

sanskrit: sa tan na mamṛṣe vīraḥ śatror vijayam āhave tato 'sya gadayā dāntān hayān sarvān apātayat
english: The hero could not brook this triumph of his foe in the fray; and so with his mace he struck down all the well-trained horses of his enemy.

sanskrit: śalyas tu nakulaṃ vīraḥ svasrīyaṃ priyam ātmanaḥ vivyādha prahasan bāṇair lāḍayan kopayann iva
english: And the hero Śalya, smiling, pierced with his arrows Nakula, his own beloved sister's son, as if caressing him, yet provoking him.

sanskrit: tasyāśvān ātapatraṃ ca dhvajaṃ sūtam atho dhanuḥ nipātya nakulaḥ saṃkhye śaṅkhaṃ dadhmau pratāpavān
english: But the valorous Nakula, having brought down his horses, his parasol, his banner, his charioteer, and his bow, blew his conch upon the field.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭaketuḥ kṛpenāstāñ chittvā bahuvidhāñ śarān kṛpaṃ vivyādha saptatyā lakṣma cāsyāharat tribhiḥ
english: Dhṛṣṭaketu, having cut down the many arrows loosed by Kṛpa, pierced Kṛpa with seventy shafts and with three struck away his emblem.

sanskrit: taṃ kṛpaḥ śaravarṣeṇa mahatā samavākirat nivārya ca raṇe vipro dhṛṣṭaketum ayodhayat
english: Kṛpa overwhelmed him with a great rain of arrows, and the brahmin, checking him in battle, fought on against Dhṛṣṭaketu.

sanskrit: sātyakiḥ kṛtavarmāṇaṃ nārācena stanāntare viddhvā vivyādha saptatyā punar anyaiḥ smayann iva
english: Sātyaki, piercing Kṛtavarman in the breast with an iron shaft, smiling as it were, pierced him again with seventy other arrows.

sanskrit: saptasaptatibhir bhojas taṃ viddhvā niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ nākampayata śaineyaṃ śīghro vāyur ivācalam
english: The Bhoja chief, piercing him with seventy-seven whetted arrows, could no more shake the grandson of Śini than a swift wind shakes a mountain.

sanskrit: senāpatiḥ suśarmāṇaṃ śīghraṃ marmasv atāḍayat sa cāpi taṃ tomareṇa jatrudeśe atāḍayat
english: The commander Dhṛṣṭadyumna swiftly struck Suśarman in his vital parts, and Suśarman in turn struck him with a lance upon the collarbone.

sanskrit: vaikartanaṃ tu samare virāṭaḥ pratyavārayat saha matsyair mahāvīryais tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: And Virāṭa, together with the mighty Matsyas, held back Vaikartana in the fight, and that seemed a marvel.

sanskrit: tat pauruṣam abhūt tatra sūtaputrasya dāruṇam yat sainyaṃ vārayām āsa śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: Terrible there was the prowess of the charioteer's son, in that he held back that whole army with his smooth-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: drupadas tu svayaṃ rājā bhagadattena saṃgataḥ tayor yuddhaṃ mahārāja citrarūpam ivābhavat bhūtānāṃ trāsajananaṃ cakrāte 'straviśāradau
english: And King Drupada himself closed with Bhagadatta; their combat, O great king, was as a wondrous spectacle, and those two masters of weaponry wrought a thing that struck terror into all creatures.

sanskrit: bhūriśravā raṇe rājan yājñaseniṃ mahāratham mahatā sāyakaughena chādayām āsa vīryavān
english: In the battle, O king, the valiant Bhūriśravas covered the great warrior, the son of Yajñasena, with a vast flood of arrows.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī tu tataḥ kruddhaḥ saumadattiṃ viśāṃ pate navatyā sāyakānāṃ tu kampayām āsa bhārata
english: But Śikhaṇḍin then, enraged, O lord of peoples, made the son of Somadatta tremble with ninety arrows, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: rākṣasau bhīmakarmāṇau haiḍimbālambusāv ubhau cakrāte 'tyadbhutaṃ yuddhaṃ parasparavadhaiṣiṇau
english: The two rākṣasas of dreadful deeds, the son of Hiḍimbā and Alambusa, both seeking each other's death, waged a most wondrous battle.

sanskrit: māyāśatasṛjau dṛptau māyābhir itaretaram antarhitau ceratus tau bhṛśaṃ vismayakāriṇau
english: Proud conjurers of a hundred illusions, by their illusions each vanished from the other, and the two ranged about, working great amazement.

sanskrit: cekitāno 'nuvindena yuyudhe tv atibhairavam yathā devāsure yuddhe balaśakrau mahābalau
english: Cekitāna fought most fearsomely with Anuvinda, as in the war of gods and demons the mighty Bala and Śakra once fought.

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇaḥ kṣatradevena vimardam akarod bhṛśam yathā viṣṇuḥ purā rājan hiraṇyākṣeṇa saṃyuge
english: Lakṣmaṇa made a fierce clash with Kṣatradeva, as Viṣṇu of old, O king, did with Hiraṇyākṣa in battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ prajavitāśvena vidhivat kalpitena ca rathenābhyapatad rājan saubhadraṃ pauravo nadan
english: Then with horses urged to full speed and a chariot fitly equipped, the Paurava, O king, rushed roaring upon the son of Subhadrā.

sanskrit: tato 'bhiyāya tvarito yuddhākāṅkṣī mahābalaḥ tena cakre mahad yuddham abhimanyur ariṃdamaḥ
english: And the mighty Abhimanyu, that tamer of foes, eager for battle, swiftly advanced and waged a great fight with him.

sanskrit: pauravas tv atha saubhadraṃ śaravrātair avākirat tasyārjunir dhvajaṃ chatraṃ dhanuś corvyām apātayat
english: The Paurava then showered the son of Subhadrā with masses of arrows, but Arjuna's son brought down his banner, his parasol, and his bow to the earth.

sanskrit: saubhadraḥ pauravaṃ tv anyair viddhvā saptabhir āśugaiḥ pañcabhis tasya vivyādha hayān sūtaṃ ca sāyakaiḥ
english: And the son of Subhadrā, piercing the Paurava with seven other swift shafts, struck his horses and his charioteer with five more arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃharṣayan senāṃ siṃhavad vinadan muhuḥ samādattārjunis tūrṇaṃ pauravāntakaraṃ śaram
english: Then, gladdening his own army and roaring again and again like a lion, the son of Arjuna swiftly took up an arrow that would make an end of the Paurava.

sanskrit: dvābhyāṃ śarābhyāṃ hārdikyaś cakarta saśaraṃ dhanuḥ tad utsṛjya dhanuś chinnaṃ saubhadraḥ paravīrahā udbabarha sitaṃ khaḍgam ādadānaḥ śarāvaram
english: But the son of Hṛdika, with two arrows, cut asunder his bow with its fitted shaft; and the son of Subhadrā, slayer of hostile heroes, casting aside the severed bow, drew his bright sword and took up his shield.

sanskrit: sa tenānekatāreṇa carmaṇā kṛtahastavat bhrāntāsir acaran mārgān darśayan vīryam ātmanaḥ
english: With that shield set with many stars, like one of practiced hand, he ranged the sword-paths with whirling blade, displaying his own valor.

sanskrit: bhrāmitaṃ punar udbhrāntam ādhūtaṃ punar ucchritam carmanistriṃśayo rājan nirviśeṣam adṛśyata
english: Now whirled, now whirled aloft, now shaken, now upraised again—the shield and the sword, O king, were seen as though there were no difference between them.

sanskrit: sa pauravarathasyeṣām āplutya sahasā nadan pauravaṃ ratham āsthāya keśapakṣe parāmṛśat
english: Leaping suddenly with a roar onto the pole of the Paurava's chariot, he mounted the Paurava's car and seized him by the locks of his hair.

sanskrit: jaghānāsya padā sūtam asināpātayad dhvajam vikṣobhyāmbhonidhiṃ tārkṣyas taṃ nāgam iva cākṣipat
english: With his foot he struck down the charioteer and with his sword felled the banner; then he flung the Paurava down as Garuḍa, churning the ocean, seizes a great serpent.

sanskrit: tam ākalitakeśāntaṃ dadṛśuḥ sarvapārthivāḥ ukṣāṇam iva siṃhena pātyamānam acetanam
english: All the kings beheld him, his hair clutched fast and senseless, being borne down like a bull brought down by a lion.

sanskrit: tam ārjunivaśaṃ prāptaṃ kṛṣyamāṇam anāthavat pauravaṃ patitaṃ dṛṣṭvā nāmṛṣyata jayadrathaḥ
english: Seeing the Paurava fallen into the power of Arjuna's son, dragged helplessly like a masterless thing, Jayadratha could not endure it.

sanskrit: sa barhiṇamahāvājaṃ kiṅkiṇīśatajālavat carma cādāya khaḍgaṃ ca nadan paryapatad rathāt
english: Taking up a sword and a shield decked with great peacock plumes and meshed with a hundred little bells, he leapt down from his chariot with a roar.

sanskrit: tataḥ saindhavam ālokya kārṣṇir utsṛjya pauravam utpapāta rathāt tūrṇaṃ śyenavan nipapāta ca
english: Then, beholding the lord of the Sindhus, the son of Kṛṣṇa let go the Paurava and sprang swiftly from the chariot, and swooped down like a hawk.

sanskrit: prāsapaṭṭiśanistriṃśāñ śatrubhiḥ saṃpraveritān cicchedāthāsinā kārṣṇiś carmaṇā saṃrurodha ca
english: The javelins, pikes, and swords hurled at him by his foes the son of Kṛṣṇa cut apart with his sword and warded off with his shield.

sanskrit: sa darśayitvā sainyānāṃ svabāhubalam ātmanaḥ tam udyamya mahākhaḍgaṃ carma cātha punar balī
english: Having displayed to the armies the might of his own arms, the strong one then raised aloft his great sword and his shield once more,

sanskrit: vṛddhakṣatrasya dāyādaṃ pitur atyantavairiṇam sasārābhimukhaḥ śūraḥ śārdūla iva kuñjaram
english: and the hero advanced straight upon the heir of Vṛddhakṣatra, his father's bitterest foe, as a tiger upon an elephant.

sanskrit: tau parasparam āsādya khaḍgadantanakhāyudhau hṛṣṭavat saṃprajahrāte vyāghrakesariṇāv iva
english: Closing upon each other, their swords for teeth and claws, the two struck joyfully, like a tiger and a lion.

sanskrit: saṃpāteṣv abhipāteṣu nipāteṣv asicarmaṇoḥ na tayor antaraṃ kaś cid dadarśa narasiṃhayoḥ
english: In the clashings, the onslaughts, and the descents of sword and shield, none could see any opening in those two lions among men.

sanskrit: avakṣepo 'sinirhrādaḥ śastrāntaranidarśanam bāhyāntaranipātaś ca nirviśeṣam adṛśyata
english: The flinging down, the clang of swords, the spying of an opening between the weapons, and the strokes outward and inward—all seemed as one, without distinction.

sanskrit: bāhyam ābhyantaraṃ caiva carantau mārgam uttamam dadṛśāte mahātmānau sapakṣāv iva parvatau
english: Ranging the outer and the inner along the supreme paths of swordcraft, the two great-souled ones appeared like winged mountains.

sanskrit: tato vikṣipataḥ khaḍgaṃ saubhadrasya yaśasvinaḥ śarāvaraṇapakṣānte prajahāra jayadrathaḥ
english: Then, as the illustrious son of Subhadrā was sweeping his sword across, Jayadratha smote upon the edge of his shield's rim.

sanskrit: rukmapakṣāntare saktas tasmiṃś carmaṇi bhāsvare sindhurājabaloddhūtaḥ so 'bhajyata mahān asiḥ
english: Caught in the gold-bordered rim of that gleaming shield, the great sword, wrenched by the strength of the king of the Sindhus, snapped asunder.

sanskrit: bhagnam ājñāya nistriṃśam avaplutya padāni ṣaṭ so 'dṛśyata nimeṣeṇa svarathaṃ punar āsthitaḥ
english: Knowing his sword broken, he leapt back six paces, and in the twinkling of an eye was seen mounted again upon his own chariot.

sanskrit: taṃ kārṣṇiṃ samarān muktam āsthitaṃ ratham uttamam sahitāḥ sarvarājānaḥ parivavruḥ samantataḥ
english: As the son of Kṛṣṇa, withdrawn from that single combat, stood mounted on his splendid chariot, all the kings together hemmed him in on every side.

sanskrit: tataś carma ca khaḍgaṃ ca samutkṣipya mahābalaḥ nanādārjunadāyādaḥ prekṣamāṇo jayadratham
english: Then the mighty heir of Arjuna, raising on high his shield and his sword, roared aloud, his eyes upon Jayadratha.

sanskrit: sindhurājaṃ parityajya saubhadraḥ paravīrahā tāpayām āsa tat sainyaṃ bhuvanaṃ bhāskaro yathā
english: Leaving the king of the Sindhus, the son of Subhadrā, slayer of hostile heroes, scorched that army as the sun scorches the world.

sanskrit: tasya sarvāyasīṃ śaktiṃ śalyaḥ kanakabhūṣaṇām cikṣepa samare ghorāṃ dīptām agniśikhām iva
english: At him Śalya hurled in the fight a dreadful spear, all of iron and adorned with gold, blazing like a tongue of fire.

sanskrit: tām avaplutya jagrāha sakośaṃ cākarod asim vainateyo yathā kārṣṇiḥ patantam uragottamam
english: Leaping up, the son of Kṛṣṇa caught it as Garuḍa, son of Vinatā, catches a falling serpent-prince, and he sheathed his sword.

sanskrit: tasya lāghavam ājñāya sattvaṃ cāmitatejasaḥ sahitāḥ sarvarājānaḥ siṃhanādam athānadan
english: Seeing the deftness and the courage of him of boundless splendor, all the kings together then raised a lion's roar.

sanskrit: tatas tām eva śalyasya saubhadraḥ paravīrahā mumoca bhujavīryeṇa vaiḍūryavikṛtājirām
english: Then that very spear, its haft wrought with cat's-eye gems, the son of Subhadrā, slayer of hostile heroes, loosed back at Śalya by the strength of his arm.

sanskrit: sā tasya ratham āsādya nirmuktabhujagopamā jaghāna sūtaṃ śalyasya rathāc cainam apātayat
english: Reaching his chariot like a serpent loosed from its slough, it struck down Śalya's charioteer and hurled him from the car.

sanskrit: tato virāṭadrupadau dhṛṣṭaketur yudhiṣṭhiraḥ sātyakiḥ kekayā bhīmo dhṛṣṭadyumnaśikhaṇḍinau yamau ca draupadeyāś ca sādhu sādhv iti cukruśuḥ
english: Then Virāṭa and Drupada, Dhṛṣṭaketu, Yudhiṣṭhira, Sātyaki, the Kekayas, Bhīma, Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin, the twins, and the sons of Draupadī cried out, "Well done! Well done!"

sanskrit: bāṇaśabdāś ca vividhāḥ siṃhanādāś ca puṣkalāḥ prādurāsan harṣayantaḥ saubhadram apalāyinam tan nāmṛṣyanta putrās te śatror vijayalakṣaṇam
english: Manifold twangings of bows and abundant lion-roars arose, gladdening the son of Subhadrā who never fled; but your sons could not endure that mark of triumph in their foe.

sanskrit: athainaṃ sahasā sarve samantān niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ abhyākiran mahārāja jaladā iva parvatam
english: Then all of them at once, O great king, showered him with whetted arrows from every side, as rain-clouds drench a mountain.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ ca priyam anvicchan sūtasya ca parābhavāt ārtāyanir amitraghnaḥ kruddhaḥ saubhadram abhyayāt
english: And seeking to do them a pleasure, and stung by the defeat of his charioteer, the son of Ārtāyana, slayer of foes, advanced in wrath upon the son of Subhadrā.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca bahūni suvicitrāṇi dvaṃdvayuddhāni saṃjaya tvayoktāni niśamyāhaṃ spṛhayāmi sacakṣuṣām
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Hearing of the many wondrous single combats you have told of, Saṃjaya, I envy those who have eyes to see.

sanskrit: āścaryabhūtaṃ lokeṣu kathayiṣyanti mānavāḥ kurūṇāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca yuddhaṃ devāsuropamam
english: As a marvel in all the worlds will men tell of this war of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas, like the war of gods and demons.

sanskrit: na hi me tṛptir astīha śṛṇvato yuddham uttamam tasmād ārtāyaner yuddhaṃ saubhadrasya ca śaṃsa me
english: For I have no surfeit in hearing of this surpassing battle; therefore tell me of the combat of the son of Ārtāyana and the son of Subhadrā.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca sāditaṃ prekṣya yantāraṃ śalyaḥ sarvāyaṣīṃ gadām samutkṣipya nadan kruddhaḥ pracaskanda rathottamāt
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing his charioteer struck down, Śalya, raising aloft a wholly iron mace and roaring in wrath, leapt from his splendid chariot.

sanskrit: taṃ dīptam iva kālāgniṃ daṇḍahastam ivāntakam javenābhyapatad bhīmaḥ pragṛhya mahatīṃ gadām
english: At him—blazing like the fire of doom, like Death with staff in hand—Bhīma rushed swiftly, gripping his great mace.

sanskrit: saubhadro 'py aśaniprakhyāṃ pragṛhya mahatīṃ gadām ehy ehīty abravīc chalyaṃ yatnād bhīmena vāritaḥ
english: The son of Subhadrā too, seizing a mighty mace like the thunderbolt, cried, "Come on, come on!" to Śalya, but with effort Bhīma held him back.

sanskrit: vārayitvā tu saubhadraṃ bhīmasenaḥ pratāpavān śalyam āsādya samare tasthau girir ivācalaḥ
english: Having checked the son of Subhadrā, the valorous Bhīmasena, advancing upon Śalya in the fray, stood firm as an unshaken mountain.

sanskrit: tathaiva madrarājo 'pi bhīmaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahābalam sasārābhimukhas tūrṇaṃ śārdūla iva kuñjaram
english: And likewise the king of the Madras, beholding the mighty Bhīma, advanced swiftly straight upon him, as a tiger upon an elephant.

sanskrit: tatas tūryaninādāś ca śaṅkhānāṃ ca sahasraśaḥ siṃhanādāś ca saṃjajñur bherīṇāṃ ca mahāsvanāḥ
english: Then the blare of trumpets and the sound of conches by the thousand, lion-roars, and the great booming of kettledrums arose together.

sanskrit: paśyatāṃ śataśo hy āsīd anyonyasamacetasām pāṇḍavānāṃ kurūṇāṃ ca sādhu sādhv iti nisvanaḥ
english: And among the hundreds of onlookers, Pāṇḍavas and Kurus alike of equal mind, there arose the cry, "Well done! Well done!"

sanskrit: na hi madrādhipād anyaḥ sarvarājasu bhārata soḍhum utsahate vegaṃ bhīmasenasya saṃyuge
english: For among all the kings, O Bhārata, none save the lord of the Madras could endure the onset of Bhīmasena in battle.

sanskrit: tathā madrādhipasyāpi gadāvegaṃ mahātmanaḥ soḍhum utsahate loke ko 'nyo yudhi vṛkodarāt
english: And likewise, who else in the world but Vṛkodara could endure in battle the mace-onset of the great-souled lord of the Madras?

sanskrit: paṭṭair jāmbūnadair baddhā babhūva janaharṣiṇī prajajvāla tathāviddhā bhīmena mahatī gadā
english: Bound about with bands of fine gold, the great mace of Bhīma was a delight to all who saw it, and brandished thus it blazed forth.

sanskrit: tathaiva carato mārgān maṇḍalāni ca bhāgaśaḥ mahāvidyutpratīkāśā śalyasya śuśubhe gadā
english: And in like manner, as it ranged the paths and circling sweeps in turn, the mace of Śalya, resembling a great flash of lightning, shone resplendent.

sanskrit: tau vṛṣāv iva nardantau maṇḍalāni viceratuḥ āvarjitagadāśṛṅgāv ubhau śalyavṛkodarau
english: Bellowing like two bulls, the pair ranged in circling sweeps—Śalya and Vṛkodara both, their maces lowered like horns turned for the charge.
